items.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And of course I heard a lot of Tommy Dorsey’s recordings but of course Tommy was not considered a jazz player. But my trombone teacher really kind of pushed that style a lot and wanted me to listen to a lot of Dorsey records.

ctx.x: I really wasn’t aware that it was a particularly new thing, the Swing Era. All I knew is what I heard on the records. I didn’t know what came before it, years before — I just started tuning my ear into what was happening in those days. And fortunately I did grow up in what we now consider the big band era in popular music. And I listened to many, many records, besides the real old stuff back in the ‘20s, of Paul Whiteman, I listened to Benny Goodman and of course in the ‘40s the Glenn Miller Band was popular, and…

interest in the classical music. The only part of music I never really got interested in was the Opera singing. I never, well to this day I really don’t enjoy it to listen to it. But I do like the music that goes along with it see, and the orchestra I’m quite interested in. But I have an interest in the classics as well as the jazz that I picked up along the way. And I think I probably had a natural tendency to tune in on the jazz aspect of the music. I became interested in what the individuals were doing on…
